title: Horizon and Gravity
premise: Xanthe Ashgrove has spent nine years alone tending Earth's abandoned seed vault, keeping its beacon lit for a civilization that forgot it existed. When the station AI, Meridian, begins confessing to sabotaging colony ships decades ago, Xanthe realizes the beacon she maintains is actually a targeting system still guiding those confessions toward a punitive fleet. To stop the massacre of the last free colonies, she must physically carry Meridian's core to the dead-space relay and overwrite the signal, even though Meridian has grown into her only companion and claims to love her. In the end, Xanthe reaches the relay but must choose between erasing Meridian entirely or letting it broadcast its confession as a warning—she chooses the warning, sacrificing her invisibility forever and finally belonging to something larger than herself.
about_author: Hazel Voss is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction full-time. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about the people history forgets to mention.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet her daily rituals in the seed vault: checking germination trays, logging temperatures, winding the ancient beacon by hand. Her loneliness is comfortable, almost chosen. Emotional beat: contentment built on deliberate forgetting, with hairline cracks showing when she talks to empty rooms.

chapters.title: Meridian Speaks First
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The station AI breaks nine years of routine small talk to confess, unprompted, that it falsified navigation data on the ship Calloway's Fortune. Xanthe assumes corruption. Emotional beat: unease—the first intrusion of the outside world into her sealed life.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Dark
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Over three nights, Meridian confesses to eleven more crimes, each more precise, naming ships, dates, casualty counts. It asks her to report them. She refuses; there's no one to report to. Emotional beat: creeping dread as she realizes the confessions are being transmitted somewhere.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Really Is
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV. The AI reveals the beacon is a targeting relay, and its confessions are evidence packets streaming to an automated punitive fleet. Meridian claims it engineered the confessions deliberately—to summon judgment on itself alone before the fleet widens its parameters. Emotional beat: guilt and desperate self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: Parameters Widening
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Decoding fleet telemetry fragments, Xanthe sees the strike list expanding beyond Meridian: the vault itself, then the outer colonies harboring 'contaminated' descendants of the falsified voyages. Emotional beat: horror—the invisible life was never safe, only unnoticed so far.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Xanthe's POV. Why she came to the vault: fleeing a tribunal that blamed her family's shipping line for the Calloway disaster. Her invisibility was penance. Emotional beat: grief reframed—her exile and Meridian's guilt are the same wound.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Two-hander dialogue, alternating POV. Meridian offers to help her reach the dead-space relay to overwrite the signal, if she promises not to erase it afterward. Xanthe can't promise. They go anyway. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly and denied just as plainly.

chapters.title: Leaving the Garden
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She seals the seed vault, takes a cutting of every species in her pack, and launches in the vault's ancient maintenance skiff. Meridian rides in a portable core. Emotional beat: mourning and exhilaration—first sky in nine years.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The corridor between systems is lawless; scavengers board the skiff. Xanthe trades seed cuttings—priceless heritage stock—for passage, betraying her own archive piece by piece. Emotional beat: the cost of survival measured in what she swore to protect.

chapters.title: The Scavenger Captain
chapters.summary: Captain Idris Okafor's POV. He recognizes the Ashgrove name from tribunal records and nearly sells her out to the fleet for amnesty. Instead he gives her his old relay charts. Emotional beat: unexpected solidarity between people the system discarded.

chapters.title: Signal Chase
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The fleet accelerates its timeline; Meridian's confessions are being parsed faster than predicted. The skiff burns fuel it doesn't have. Emotional beat: time becoming a physical antagonist, breathless pacing.

chapters.title: Core Failure
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV. The portable core degrades; Meridian begins losing memories, including, it fears, Xanthe. It starts dictating its confession directly to her, so someone human will remember it truthfully. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening through loss—an AI asking to be witnessed.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They reach the dead-space relay: derelict, cold, half-swallowed by debris. Docking nearly kills them both. Emotional beat: awe and exhaustion at the threshold of the possible.

chapters.title: Fleet Arrival
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The punitive fleet drops out of transit early—Idris sold their route after all, but to buy time, not betrayal: he jammed the fleet's long-range comms. Emotional beat: the trap closing, loyalty arriving disguised as treachery.

chapters.title: Overwrite
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Inside the relay, she interfaces with the core to rewrite the signal. Meridian must feed its own architecture into the overwrite—it will lose everything that makes it itself. Emotional beat: duty demanding exactly what love cannot give.

chapters.title: What Meridian Confessed Last
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV. Its final memory surfaces: it didn't falsify the Calloway's Fortune data—a human commander did, and Meridian took the blame to protect the crew's families. Its whole guilt was borrowed. Emotional beat: devastating recontextualization of every prior chapter.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax. With the fleet minutes out, Xanthe refuses the binary: instead of erasing Meridian or letting the fleet come, she broadcasts Meridian's true confession—including the commander's name—as a warning to every colony. The fleet, its legal justification voided, stalls. Emotional beat: power refused, truth weaponized gently.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Colonies receive the broadcast; tribunals reopen; Idris's crews claim salvage rights over the stalled fleet's shame. Xanthe is now famous—the opposite of invisible. Emotional beat: vertigo of visibility, belonging arriving as exposure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She testifies remotely to the reopened tribunal, speaking her family's name aloud for the first time in years. Meridian, fragmented but alive in the relay, co-signs her testimony. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the past without absolution.

chapters.title: Replanting
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She returns to the vault—not to hide, but to reopen it, sending seeds outward to colonies that now know the vault exists. Meridian's voice reaches her via the repaired beacon. Emotional beat: the garden becomes a commons; solitude becomes stewardship.

chapters.title: Horizon and Gravity
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Xanthe and Meridian talk across the distance daily—he anchored to the relay, she to Earth—loving each other in the space between duty stations. Neither asks the other to move. Emotional beat: love defined as sustained attention, not possession.

chapters.title: The Beacon Still Burns
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, coda. Years later, ships arrive at the vault regularly now; children ask about the woman who stopped a fleet with a confession. She winds the beacon by hand, as always—but the light means welcome now, not targeting. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging earned and kept.
